findings.finding: Nielsen sell-out data cited by Goldman Sachs show NIVEA down 6% in Europe over the 12 weeks to 6 Sept 2026 (Vaseline +7%, Mixa +22%), while the Q3 consensus (Consumer organic -1.0%) implies NIVEA improving to roughly -4% from -6.7% in Q2 against a Q3'25 Consumer comp of +2.1%; GS models group -1.4% and NIVEA -5.5%, so the Consumer line is more likely to miss than beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 organic -4.6%, below expectations: -3.46% on 2026-04-21; H1/Q2 NIVEA -6.7% with guidance cut via ad-hoc 2026-08-03: -1.93% that day; Q3 2025 sales with a guide trim: +0.29% on 2025-10-23. Sales-only quarterlies have moved 0.3-3.5%.
findings.original_quote: Goldman nennt Auslistungen im Handel und die schwache Verbraucherstimmung als Gruende fuer den erwarteten Nivea-Rueckgang (paraphrase on page: 'Fuer Nivea prognostiziert die Bank einen Rueckgang von 5,5 Prozent'; Nielsen: Vaseline +7 %, Mixa +22 %, Nivea 'verlor 6 Prozent' in den zwoelf Wochen bis 6. September). Translation: Goldman cites retailer delistings and weak consumer sentiment; it forecasts NIVEA -5.5%; NIVEA lost 6% in Nielsen Europe in the 12 weeks to 6 September.
findings.why_not_priced: The GS note is public since 6 Oct, yet the stock rose about 11% afterwards and the Visible Alpha bar published 23 Oct still sits at -1.0% Consumer, i.e. the consensus has not moved to the sell-out data; if it were priced the bar would be near GS's -1.4% group and the stock would not have rallied above the mean target (EUR 81.20). Partly priced: the data are public and a broker's, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Management itself said NIVEA remained under short-term pressure from promotions and delistings in Europe as retailers demand price cuts, and that H1 sell-out trailed the market (Q2 call and May JPM conference) - https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/news/bz-all-rss/unternehmen-branchen/beiersdorf-kaempft-mit-bremslklotz-nivea ; offsetting: management attributed Q2 sell-in weakness partly to temporary destocking and a late sun season, which could reverse in Q3.

findings.finding: UBS (in the Dow Jones/Visible Alpha preview) expects the Consumer segment to end FY2026 at the low end of the lowered guide because Q4 faces strong prior-year comparisons; a 'lower end' qualifier in the Q3 statement would be a guidance-line negative even with the range unchanged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance cuts: 2026-03-03 FY26 outlook -20.13%; 2026-08-03 ad-hoc cut -1.93% (then +5.12% on the 2026-08-05 report); 2025-10-23 guide trim to ~2.5% +0.29%.
findings.original_quote: koennte das Consumer-Segment am Jahresende beim Umsatz sogar am unteren Rand der gesenkten Prognose landen - Translation: the Consumer segment could even end the year at the lower end of the lowered sales guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: FY Consumer consensus at -2.5% sits mid-range of 'low-single-digit decline'; if a lower-end outcome were priced the FY consensus would be nearer -3% and the stock would not have rerated 11% in three weeks. One analyst's view, not the company's, so small.

findings.finding: The stock rallied from EUR 75.40 (2 Oct) to EUR 84.12 (23 Oct), +11.6%, with no company datapoint - after a GS downgrade to Sell - and now trades above the mean analyst target (EUR 81.20, 21 analysts) and well above the cluster of 68-74 targets (GS 73, DB 70, Jefferies 74, DZ 74), so the release has to justify a relief rerating that is already in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a rally into the 2026-03 FY print (EUR ~105) the outlook drove -20%; into Q1 2026 (-3.46%) the stock had not run up. No clean precedent of a run-up into a sales-only print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; the claim is that the rerating raised the effective bar above the published Visible Alpha numbers. It largely agrees with the free control (-run_up), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Mean target EUR 81.20 / HALTEN, 21 analysts - https://de.marketscreener.com/boerse-nachrichten/ausblick-bei-beiersdorf-laeuft-nivea-weniger-geschmiert-ce785cdfdb8cf52c ; GS Sell TP 73 - https://www.teleborsa.it/DettaglioNews/93_2026-10-06_TLB/Beiersdorf-Goldman-Sachs-declassa-a-Sell-e-taglia-il-TP-con-marchio-Nivea-che-frena-la-crescita.html

findings.finding: L'Oreal's Q3 2026 (22 Oct) beat with +7.7% adjusted LFL against 5.9% consensus, with Dermatological Beauty +15.7%, which supports Beiersdorf's Derma line (Eucerin/Aquaphor, about 20% of Consumer, +7.4% organic in Q2) printing at or above its trend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Derma has been the consistent positive (H1 +7.8%) and has not stopped the stock falling on NIVEA; BEI rose +2.4% on 2026-10-23, the session after L'Oreal's release.
findings.original_quote: Une fois de plus, le marche mondial de la beaute demontre sa resilience dans un contexte difficile (L'Oreal CEO). Translation: once again the global beauty market shows its resilience in a difficult context.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: BEI's +2.4% on 23 Oct is the sympathy move. What is left is the Derma line itself, which the Visible Alpha preview only expects to show 'small gains'; a strong market for dermocosmetics argues Derma beats that. Also cuts the other way for NIVEA: a strong mass market makes NIVEA's decline share loss, not market.

findings.finding: La Prairie read-through is split: L'Oreal reported a China rebound (North Asia +14.1%) while Bernstein (19 Oct) flagged a weak China online cosmetics market; the consensus expects La Prairie to grow, and the evidence does not move that either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: La Prairie's double-digit Q1 decline contributed to the -3.46% on 2026-04-21; its Q2 return to growth was part of the +5.12% on 2026-08-05.
findings.original_quote: Bernstein verweist auf die schwache Entwicklung des chinesischen Online-Kosmetikmarkts (paraphrased on page). Translation: Bernstein points to the weak development of China's online cosmetics market.
findings.why_not_priced: Two public signals that offset; filed at 0 because the evidence is balanced, not because it is priced.

findings.finding: The share buyback is running: weekly MAR Art. 5 buyback reports were filed every Monday through 19 Oct 2026, a steady bid that cushions a negative print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Programme announced 2026-03 (up to EUR 750m); it did not prevent the -20% on 2026-03-03 or the -3.46% on 2026-04-21.
findings.why_not_priced: Known and ongoing; it matters only as a cushion on the day, so it is sized near zero.

baseline_tension: The findings lean negative and agree with the free control (-run_up: +5.9% 20d, +11.6% from the 2 Oct low) while cutting slightly against priced_lean_pct (+0.01, effectively neutral with a 0.51% non-crowded short), so the scaled number is small and not far from the findings' sum.

lessons_applied: 'Understatement is the systematic error' / 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 4.5 to 5.0. The Q3 numbers are new (no pre-release), but the guide is most likely reiterated (2.3% median) and sales-only quarterlies here have moved 0.3-3.5%, so it stays below the 7% base.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the NIVEA finding rests on broker-relayed Nielsen data, public since 6 Oct, so it went from -1.0 to -0.8.
'Positioning is the thing to beat, not to agree with': the run-up finding agrees with the free control, so it went from -0.8 to -0.5.
'A German ad-hoc before the print may have pre-released the number': checked; the only ad-hoc (2026-08-03) covered H1 and the guide, not Q3, so nothing was zeroed.
